conviction_note: Q3 is fully pre-released: the 14 Oct trading update gave volumes and realised prices, and the company-compiled consensus total income of USD 3,812m is exactly the arithmetic of those numbers. So the release turns on the FY production guide, which can only narrow (year to date about 385 mboepd against a 380-400 range), and on an impairment reversal that is likely but one-off. With a 13% October run-up, results-day beats sold before (-3.91% on the Q1 2026 EBIT beat) and no anchored positioning, the lean is slightly negative: p_up 47 on a 3.3% scale. print_vs_bar (+8, headline EBIT, inferred from the reversal) and the move disagree in sign because a one-off beat is sold.

findings.finding: The Q2 impairment test priced H2-2026 oil at USD 73.9 and 2027 at 71.1 and booked a USD 625m impairment of Valhall intangibles, which are reversible. Brent traded around USD 100-107 at the end of Q3, so the Q3 test likely reverses part of that against a consensus impairment line of (15), producing a headline EBIT and net-profit beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 carried a USD 522m reversal and EBIT of 2.65bn against a 1.956bn Bloomberg consensus; the stock fell 3.91% that day (baseline history, 2026-05-07). Q2's 625m impairment day was -0.65%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus impairments for Q3 are (15) USDm (akerbp.com/en/investor/analyst, 21 Oct), so the compiled estimates do not carry a reversal. If they did, consensus EBIT would be about 3.3bn rather than 2.848bn. It is below-EBITDA accounting with no path to the guide, and a beat made of a one-off is sold, so it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: Late-September Brent around USD 105.6 (https://telanganatoday.com/brent-crude-hovers-around-106-amid-hopes-of-strait-of-hormuz-deal, 2026-09-25); Q3 realised liquids at USD 100.6 in the company's own trading update.

findings.finding: Year-to-date production is about 385.4 mboepd (Q1 398.4, Q2 383.6, Q3 374.3) against a 380-400 range, so the FY guide can only narrow toward the lower half. Peer Vår Energi took its FY output to the low end of its range on 21 Oct.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 narrowed the range up (370-400 to 380-400) and raised capex; stock -0.65%. Feb 2025 strategy update with a lower output outlook: -3.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: consensus FY26 production of 386 already implies Q4 at about 388, inside the range. The unpriced part is only the tail where management says 'low end' (about 380, which needs only 364 in Q4) rather than lower half. If the market expected a low-end guide, the stock would not have run 13% into the print and consensus would sit near 380, not 386.
findings.independence: Vår Energi Q3, 21 Oct 2026: FY26 output at the low end of 390-410 because of operational problems (https://www.oedigital.com/news/543811-vaar-energi-doubles-third-quarter-profit).

findings.finding: The stock ran from 338.4 (2 Oct) to 384.8 (+13% in 20 sessions), above the last sourced broker targets (DNB NOK 370 in July; average about NOK 329 in mid-August), into a release whose quarter is fully pre-released. Peer Vår Energi's strong Q3 with a dividend raise moved -0.11%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last two results days after up-moves were -3.91% (May 2026) and -0.65% (Jul 2026); the Oct 2025 and Feb 2026 results days were +3.3% and +4.44%.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up itself is the free control and is mostly in the price. What is filed is that the release adds nothing to the quarter while the price sits above sourced targets, so the print has little to justify the move. The targets are stale (July and August) and likely raised since, so this is sized small.
